world.title: Uganda, U.S. Sign $1.7 Billion Five-Year Health Deal
world.description:
Uganda and the United States have signed a five-year, $1.7 billion health agreement running from 2026 to 2030, with a major shift towards direct government-to-government financing.
The funding will support disease prevention and detection, emergency response and other health programmes, with money increasingly channelled through Uganda's Ministry of Finance rather than external organisations. The wider co-investment package is valued at $2.3 billion, including Uganda's commitment to increase domestic health financing by more than $500 million over the period.
Both governments said the arrangement would strengthen national ownership, align aid with Uganda's priorities and improve the sustainability of health programmes.

business.title: Effects of tunnel aspect ratio on the temperature profile near fire field in tunnel under natural ventilation: a numerical investigation and analysis
business.description: The ceiling temperature distribution near fire field is a critical characteristic parameter for assessing the risk and dynamic characteristics of a tunnel fire. Nevertheless, the temperature of the ceiling jet propelled by the weak and strong has not been studied in relation to the tunnel aspect ratio in previous research. In this study, a series of numerical simulations are performed to investigate the vertical and transverse temperature distribution under the ceiling, with the heat release rate and tunnel aspect ratios being adjusted. It is found that there is an obvious difference between the vertical temperature variation above the fire source and other positions, as the varying tunnel aspect ratio. Significant differences in the transverse temperature decay behavior of the ceiling jet generated by strong and weak plumes are found. Furthermore, a quantified analysis of the transverse temperature distribution for the faint and strong plume is performed. As a result, two empirical models of transverse temperature distribution were postulated for the weak and strong plumes, respectively. The current study results lead to a more in-depth understanding of the fire characteristics of the tunnel with large aspect ratio, as well as to the optimization of fire detection and emergency ventilation.

science.title: Cross-modal audio-text attention for multimodal multitask speech emotion recognition in low-resource Urdu
science.description: Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) in low-resource languages remains challenging due to limited annotated data, speaker variability, and the multimodal nature of emotional expression. This paper repositions established components wav2vec 2.0, XLM-R, cross-modal attention, and multitask affective modeling into a framework jointly validated across speaker-independent, cross-lingual zero-shot, and attribution-faithfulness generalization for Urdu, a combination not jointly reported in prior Urdu SER work. The proposed multimodal multitask model achieves 91.3% emotion recognition accuracy on the Urdu Speech Emotion Corpus (UrSEC), outperforming strong audio-only and text-only baselines, with joint valence-arousal learning consistently improving over emotion-only training. Speaker-independent evaluation shows a performance drop relative to random-split testing but confirms substantial robustness to speaker-specific bias. Cross-lingual zero-shot evaluation on English datasets yields 80.2 ± 1.3% (IEMOCAP) to 86.3 ± 0.9% (CREMA-D) accuracy without fine-tuning, indicating substantial cross-lingual transfer, though this alone does not establish full language-neutrality. All performance gains are statistically validated across multiple runs, and attention/Integrated Gradients analyses, supported by quantitative faithfulness testing, show the model relies on emotionally salient acoustic regions and Urdu tokens rather than spurious correlations.

science.title: Toward long-term stability of SAW sensor interface electronics with minimized heat generation and baseline fluctuation
science.description: Three different interface architectures were developed to convert changes in surface acoustic wave (SAW) velocity, generated by a two-port SAW delay line with a UV-C sensing material, into measurable frequency shifts for real-time monitoring and analysis. The system includes an oscillator, multiplexer (MUX), mixer, low-pass filter (LPF), comparator, field-programmable gate array (FPGA), and a PC-based visualization unit. The three architectures were evaluated based on signal stability, noise performance, baseline drift, and frequency detection accuracy. All designs demonstrated low noise, minimal heat generation, and stable long-term operation with negligible baseline fluctuations. Depending on the specific sensor application, the most appropriate architecture can be selected and integrated into the system. Each architecture provides a compact and reliable solution for high-resolution SAW sensor signal processing and monitoring. Additionally, a visualization algorithm was implemented to display real-time data and provide warning alerts using color-coded indicators around the display window.
